articles.title: Two-week monitor after unexplained fainting identifies life-threatening heart conditions
articles.summary_3_sentences: A trial presented at ESC Congress reported that 14-day wearable heart monitoring after ER visits for unexplained fainting improved detection of serious heart conditions. The report concerns diagnostic follow-up for patients whose fainting cause is not immediately clear.

articles.title: Heart, body and mind--the first ESC Guidelines highlight the many benefits of cardiac rehabilitation
articles.summary_3_sentences: The European Society of Cardiology published its first guidelines on cardiac rehabilitation in the European Heart Journal. The guidelines emphasize physical, psychological and overall health benefits for people with heart disease.

articles.title: Fractional exhaled nitric oxide elevated in pediatric chest tightness-variant asthma
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Frontiers in Pediatrics study found higher fractional exhaled nitric oxide levels and lower small-airway function measures in children with chest tightness-variant asthma. The findings concern pediatric asthma assessment and airway inflammation markers.

articles.title: New global definition of myocardial infarction aims to improve diagnosis, treatment and patient understanding
articles.summary_3_sentences: Four major cardiac societies released the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction. The definition aims to improve classification, diagnosis, treatment decisions and patient understanding of heart attacks.

articles.title: New guidelines recommend all patients with heart disease are tested for kidney disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: New ESC guidelines developed with the European Renal Association recommend kidney disease testing for all patients with heart disease. The guidance addresses management where cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease overlap.

articles.title: People who could benefit from blood pressure medication may be missing out on treatment
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research presented at ESC Congress suggested that some people with only slightly elevated heart disease risk may still benefit from blood pressure-lowering treatment. The report focuses on potential undertreatment in hypertension prevention.

articles.title: Statins cut first heart attack and stroke risk 30% after age 70
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that statin use after age 70 was associated with a 30% reduction in first heart attack and stroke risk. The summary frames statins as cholesterol-lowering drugs commonly used up to age 75.

articles.title: Major changes made to the ESC Guidelines on heart failure
articles.summary_3_sentences: The European Society of Cardiology published updated heart failure guidelines in the European Heart Journal. The changes reflect evolving understanding and treatment advances in heart failure care.

articles.title: Machine learning model identifies heart failure with reduced ejection fraction using routine lab indicators
articles.summary_3_sentences: A 13-indicator routine laboratory model showed moderate ability to distinguish heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. The study was published in Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine.

articles.title: Breast cancer survivors could avoid lifelong heart medication, research suggests
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study presented at ESC Congress suggested some breast cancer survivors with treatment-related heart dysfunction may safely stop heart medication after recovery. The finding applies to selected patients and does not imply all survivors can discontinue therapy.

articles.title: Cardiologist referrals improve cholesterol levels in prostate cancer patients, but may not be necessary for all
articles.summary_3_sentences: An international study found that routine internist or cardiologist referrals improved cholesterol levels in men with prostate cancer. The referrals did not reduce heart attacks, strokes, heart failure or cardiovascular deaths in the reported analysis.

articles.title: Implantable cardioverter-defibrillators may benefit certain younger patients with mild-moderate heart dysfunction
articles.summary_3_sentences: A long-term trial reported potential benefit from implantable cardioverter-defibrillators in certain younger patients with mild-to-moderate heart dysfunction. The findings were presented at ESC 2026 and published in JAMA.

articles.title: Monoclonal antibody targeting interleukin-6 achieves sustained reductions in inflammation biomarkers through six months
articles.summary_3_sentences: The investigational anti-IL-6 antibody pacibekitug reduced inflammation-related biomarkers through six months. The report involved patients with chronic kidney disease and elevated inflammatory risk linked to heart disease.

articles.title: Reducing antibiotic courses by two weeks could be possible in patients with infective endocarditis
articles.summary_3_sentences: A response-tailored strategy reduced antibiotic duration by two weeks in patients with left-sided infective endocarditis. The summary states that safety was not compromised in the reported study.

articles.title: No benefit of heart CT scan in patients with acute chest pain, trial finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A trial found that coronary CT angiography did not reduce heart attacks or cardiac death over three years in acute chest pain patients after heart attack had been excluded. The findings were presented at ESC Congress.

articles.title: Silent artery plaques may appear in one in 13 adults before age 30
articles.summary_3_sentences: An international study found detectable atherosclerosis in apparently healthy young adults before age 30. The report suggests silent plaques may be more common early in life than previously recognized.

articles.title: Long-term melatonin use linked to 90% higher heart failure risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: A preliminary study linked long-term melatonin use in people with chronic insomnia to a roughly 90% higher five-year heart failure risk. The report notes that the association does not prove causation.

articles.title: Turmeric compound may protect blood vessels from diabetes damage
articles.summary_3_sentences: In rats with type 1 diabetes, curcumin reduced inflammation and improved vascular signaling and blood vessel health. The report is preclinical and states that human trials are still needed.

articles.title: Cannabis use linked to 37% higher stroke risk in massive study
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large analysis linked recreational drug use with stroke risk, including a 37% higher risk associated with cannabis. Cocaine and amphetamines were also associated with substantially higher stroke risks.

articles.title: Peppermint oil lowers blood pressure in just 20 days
articles.summary_3_sentences: Adults with mildly high blood pressure who took peppermint oil twice daily for 20 days had lower systolic blood pressure than placebo recipients. The report frames peppermint oil as a possible adjunct option needing further study.

articles.title: Blood Pressure Drugs Linked to Kidney Risk in Diabetes
articles.summary_3_sentences: A commonly prescribed class of blood pressure drugs was associated with higher risk of serious kidney problems in people with diabetes. The visible summary reports an association rather than establishing causation.

articles.title: This 10-cent heart drug cuts hospitalizations by 25%
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research suggested low-dose digoxin may reduce heart-failure hospitalizations by about 25%. The article highlights renewed interest in an inexpensive older heart drug.

topic_groups.topic: Metabolic Health, Diabetes, Obesity and Nutrition

articles.title: Neighborhood walkability linked to lower type 2 diabetes risk in women with prior gestational diabetes
articles.summary_3_sentences: A New York City study linked more walkable neighborhoods to lower postpartum type 2 diabetes risk among women with prior gestational diabetes. The association varied by socioeconomic factors including Medicaid coverage and neighborhood deprivation.

articles.title: Early initiation of statins after diagnosis of type 2 diabetes associated with a lower risk of dementia
articles.summary_3_sentences: Early statin initiation after type 2 diabetes diagnosis was associated with lower dementia risk. The study was presented at ESC Congress 2026 and published in The Lancet Regional Health - Europe.

articles.title: Common supplements rival antibiotics for severe gum disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: A year-long study found omega-3 plus low-dose aspirin matched antibiotics for severe gum disease treatment goals. The result may inform approaches that reduce antibiotic reliance in some patients.

articles.title: Researchers unveil sustainable spirulina solution to vitamin B12 deficiency
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers produced Spirulina containing biologically active vitamin B12 at levels described as comparable to beef. The method uses controlled lighting to address conventional Spirulina's inactive B12 problem.

articles.title: Keto diet cut liver fat by 67% in a clinical trial
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a clinical trial of people with obesity, prediabetes and fatty liver disease, a ketogenic diet reduced liver fat more than Mediterranean or low-fat diets. All groups lost similar weight, but the keto group had a larger liver-fat reduction.

articles.title: Scientists tested 212 plant-based meat alternatives. Every one contained fungal toxins
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin in 212 tested UK plant-based meat alternatives and drinks. Concentrations were below EU guideline levels, but cumulative exposure was raised as a question.

articles.title: Study tests if longevity methods slow signs of aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study compared pharmaceutical and lifestyle interventions by their effects on epigenetic signs of aging. The visible summary states that both types of interventions were among the most effective approaches.

articles.title: Coffee May Improve Many Aspects of Health
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports possible coffee benefits for heart health, metabolism and body composition. The summary provides broad associations without specific outcome details.

articles.title: Vitamin C won't prevent most colds, but it may do one small thing
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reviews evidence that vitamin C does not prevent most colds. Regular use may slightly shorten or lessen severe symptoms.

articles.title: Scientists may have found a shortcut to calorie restriction's anti-aging benefits
articles.summary_3_sentences: Moderate calorie restriction lowered the immune protein C3, which was linked to age-related inflammation. Blocking C3 reduced inflammation in mice, suggesting a possible route to mimic some calorie-restriction effects.

articles.title: Your genes may decide whether a low-carb diet sends cholesterol soaring
articles.summary_3_sentences: A low-carb diet may raise LDL cholesterol more sharply in people genetically predisposed to high cholesterol, especially with high saturated-fat intake. The report highlights genetic variability in diet responses.

articles.title: Too much or too little sleep may make your body age faster
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers analyzing biological aging clocks found lowest aging levels among people sleeping about 6.4 to 7.8 hours daily. Shorter and longer sleep were linked to faster aging and multiple health conditions.

articles.title: Experimental compound helps burn fat without muscle loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, TOFA increased energy use, reduced body fat without major muscle loss and improved metabolic markers. The preclinical compound also showed stronger effects when combined with GLP-1 drugs.

articles.title: Gut bacteria may unlock a hidden benefit of vegetables
articles.summary_3_sentences: Gut bacteria can transform vegetable-derived nitrate and plant-based iron into molecules linked to cardiovascular and metabolic benefits. The reported evidence includes experimental models.

articles.title: Exercise may work better for keeping weight off than losing it
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that exercise may be more important for preventing weight regain than for initial weight loss. Proposed mechanisms include preserving muscle, supporting metabolism and improving appetite and glucose regulation.

articles.title: 3 minutes of sprinting does something 90 minutes of exercise does not
articles.summary_3_sentences: Six 30-second sprints changed many more measured blood proteins and metabolites than 90 minutes of moderate cycling. Several affected proteins were associated with lower metabolic disease risks.

articles.title: This weight-loss hormone may protect the liver even without weight loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported that GDF15 may activate a brain-to-liver pathway that calms liver inflammation and scarring. The mechanism involves glucocorticoid release and may be partly independent of weight loss.

articles.title: Type 1 Diabetes Helped with Fasting, not Calorie Counting
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Diabetes Care study examined intermittent fasting in people with type 1 diabetes. The visible summary reports benefit from fasting rather than calorie counting.

articles.title: Ozempic does something unexpected to the brain's hunger neurons
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, Ozempic was reported to activate hunger-linked neurons that may be important for sustained fat loss. The preclinical finding could identify targets for obesity-drug development.

articles.title: Coffee drinkers have less fat, more muscle, and surprising hormone differences
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Finnish study found higher coffee intake was associated with less total and abdominal fat, more muscle and healthier metabolic markers. The report describes associations despite similar BMI levels.

articles.title: Daily Fruit Juice Reduces Symptoms of Depression
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that adding daily 100% fruit juice or a smoothie may reduce depression symptoms. The dietary context is a fruit- and vegetable-rich diet.

articles.title: The bacteria that make cheese taste so good may also benefit your gut
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers studying artisan cheeses found microbes involved in flavor may also produce compounds linked to gut-health benefits. The article notes possible links to inflammation, cholesterol regulation and appetite control.

articles.title: When gut microbes run low on fiber, they may start eating you
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported that low-fiber conditions may prompt gut microbes to consume proteins from the protective mucus lining. Fiber suppressed this process, while indigestible plant proteins supported beneficial compounds.

articles.title: Full-Fat Dairy May Be Healthier Than Previously Thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports findings suggesting that avoiding full-fat dairy may not always be necessary. The visible summary does not provide a specific outcome measure.

articles.title: Drinking orange juice every day may change thousands of genes
articles.summary_3_sentences: Regular orange juice intake was reported to influence genes tied to inflammation, blood pressure, metabolism and blood sugar control. The article also notes possible cholesterol, vascular and microbiome effects.

articles.title: A surprising brain discovery could help explain why we overeat fatty foods
articles.summary_3_sentences: A protein in appetite-controlling brain cells may help prevent overeating and obesity when high-fat foods are available. The report also highlights sex differences that may affect obesity risk and drug responses.

articles.title: Pill-Based GLP-1 Drug Cuts Weight by Up to 12.1%
articles.summary_3_sentences: Aleniglipron, an oral GLP-1 drug, helped adults with obesity or overweight lose up to 12.1% of body weight over 36 weeks. The report concerns a pill-based weight-loss therapy.

articles.title: New GLP-1 pill delivers up to 12% weight loss in 36 weeks
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental once-daily oral GLP-1 small molecule helped people with obesity or overweight lose up to 12.1% of body weight in 36 weeks. The report notes potential production advantages over injectable drugs.

articles.title: Potatoes may have given Indigenous Andeans a digestive superpower
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers linked potato-based diets in the Andes to high copy numbers of a starch-digestion gene in Indigenous Peruvians. The report presents evidence that diet shaped human genetic evolution.

articles.title: A daily glass of fruit juice was linked to lower depression scores
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a small four-week trial, adding 100% fruit juice or a smoothie to a healthier diet was linked to lower depression scores. The finding suggests a dietary association that needs further study.

articles.title: Your brain may be wired to regain lost weight
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article explains biological mechanisms that can promote weight regain after dieting, including hunger, cravings and reduced energy use. It also notes that GLP-1-related drugs can reduce appetite signals while treatment continues.

articles.title: Twice-daily radiation linked to better quality of life in lung cancer trial
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports quality-of-life findings from the NRG-LU005 limited-stage small-cell lung cancer trial. Earlier results found that adding atezolizumab to concurrent chemoradiation did not improve overall survival.

articles.title: Next generation theranostic pair offers new strategy to detect and treat metastatic kidney cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: A radiotheranostic pair, 68Ga/177Lu-NYM096, was reported to identify tumors and deliver targeted radiotherapy in metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma. The article describes the approach as safe and feasible for end-stage disease.

articles.title: Predicting Melanoma Immunotherapy Treatment Success
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article focuses on predicting which late-stage melanoma patients will respond successfully to immunotherapy. It notes that about half of patients do not achieve the same benefit.

articles.title: Henlius and Sandoz Collaborate on Oncology Biosimilars Partnership
articles.summary_3_sentences: Shanghai Henlius Biotech and Sandoz announced a collaboration on oncology biosimilars. The companies plan to develop about 10 biosimilar products or components.

articles.title: Smart nanoparticles light up brain cancer and destroy what surgery misses
articles.summary_3_sentences: Smart nanoparticles were designed to illuminate glioblastoma cells during surgery and destroy residual cancer afterward. In mice, the treatment prevented recurrence and produced 60-day survival, but it has not been tested in humans.

articles.title: Eating more ultra-processed foods may raise prostate cancer risk by 30%
articles.summary_3_sentences: A nationally representative study of more than 17,000 U.S. men linked higher ultra-processed food intake to 24% to 31% higher prostate cancer risk. The analysis adjusted for several demographic and health factors.

articles.title: Experimental drug targets "undruggable" cancer protein
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental drug disrupted activity of MYC, a cancer protein described as difficult to target. The report focuses on the drug's ability to affect MYC activity.

articles.title: Orphan Diseases and Their Impact on Anticancer Drugs
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses orphan diseases in relation to anticancer drugs and the Orphan Drug Act. The visible summary provides policy context rather than a specific clinical outcome.

articles.title: Supercharged "natural killer" cells could be a powerful new cancer weapon
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers prepared tissue-resident natural killer cells that penetrated solid tumors and maintained antitumor activity. In mice, the cells slowed melanoma and head and neck tumor growth and worked better with cetuximab.

articles.title: This yeast supplement may boost cancer-fighting immunity
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, yeast beta-glucan reprogrammed early immune cells and strengthened responses against colorectal, skin and breast cancer cells. The report is preclinical and does not establish human efficacy.

articles.title: Personalized Cancer Vaccine Shows Protects from Melanoma Recurrence
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes a personalized cancer vaccine linked to protection from melanoma recurrence. It discusses a Merck and Moderna collaboration in melanoma treatment.

articles.title: Tooth count may predict survival after pancreatic cancer surgery
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of 339 pancreatic cancer surgery patients found longer survival among those with at least 21 natural teeth. Tooth loss may reflect broader factors such as inflammation, frailty and nutrition.

articles.title: A simple at-home test could cut colorectal cancer death risk by 43%
articles.summary_3_sentences: Long-term Swedish data linked participation in colorectal cancer screening to a 43% lower risk of dying from the disease. The article highlights the potential value of completing at-home screening tests.

articles.title: Colorectal Cancer Damages Nerves
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that colorectal cancer can damage nerves. The visible summary places the finding in the context of cancer progression and treatment.

articles.title: Mathematical Biomarkers Predict Prostate Cancer Outcomes
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that mathematical biomarkers may predict prostate cancer outcomes. The visible text refers to multiple anticancer treatment strategies.

articles.title: The COVID-19 vaccine may offer brain cancer patients a surprise benefit
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that a recent COVID-19 vaccine shot doubled survival time in glioblastoma patients after biopsy or surgery. The summary does not provide enough detail to establish mechanism or generalizability.

articles.title: Scientists turn probiotic bacteria into tiny drug factories for pancreatic cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: Engineered probiotic bacteria infiltrated pancreatic tumors, stimulated immune cells and slowed tumor growth in animal studies. The approach worked better when combined with chemotherapy, radiation or immunotherapy.

articles.title: Targeting Tumor 'Softness' Enhances Immunotherapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers developed a tool to detect tumor softness and linked that property to immunotherapy response. The visible summary states that targeting tumor softness enhanced immunotherapy.

articles.title: Air Pollution Alters Health Measurably Before Lung Cancer Diagnosis
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports measurable health effects from air pollution before lung cancer diagnosis, including in people who do not smoke. The visible summary frames the finding around prediagnostic changes.

articles.title: Pre-Clinical Studies Link Sugar to Ovarian Cancer Metastasis
articles.summary_3_sentences: Preclinical studies reported a link between sugar and ovarian cancer metastasis. The visible summary says the work examined cellular mechanisms related to the association.

articles.title: Vitamin C may fight cancer -- but not the way scientists once thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article distinguishes oral vitamin C supplements from intravenous vitamin C, which can reach much higher concentrations. Early studies suggest intravenous vitamin C may affect vulnerable cancer cells and treatment side effects, but the evidence remains preliminary.

articles.title: Novel Protein Drives Cancer Treatment Resistance
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a novel protein associated with resistance to cancer treatment. The article places the finding in the broader context of cancer therapy resistance.

articles.title: Immune Cells Help Tumors Grow
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that immune cells can help tumors grow. The visible summary focuses on interactions between immune cells and tumor survival.

articles.title: A simple supplement could help the immune system fight cancer and viruses
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, arginine-rich diets were linked to fewer colon tumors and milder viral infections. The preclinical report suggests arginine may influence immune warning signals relevant to cancer and infection.

topic_groups.topic: Neuroscience, Dementia, Mental Health and Pain

articles.title: HEPA air purifiers may boost brain function after just one month
articles.summary_3_sentences: Adults aged 40 and older performed faster on an executive-function test after one month using a HEPA air purifier at home. The report suggests cleaner indoor air may benefit cognition in the context of traffic-related pollution.

articles.title: Preclinical study points to cancer drugs as possible treatments for chronic nerve pain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that BRAF may contribute to chronic pain after nerve damage. BRAF inhibitors reduced pain sensitivity in preclinical models, so human relevance remains unproven.

articles.title: Magic mushrooms in palliative care: Clinicians are keen but ill-equipped
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses clinician interest in psilocybin for palliative care amid renewed research on depression, addiction and end-of-life distress. It reports that clinicians may be interested but insufficiently prepared for clinical use.

articles.title: A cancer therapy put severe rheumatoid arthritis into remission
articles.summary_3_sentences: CAR T-cell therapy reduced disease activity in six people with severe treatment-resistant rheumatoid arthritis. Three achieved medication-free remission, but larger studies are needed.

articles.title: Human brain organoids gain sense of time and space
articles.summary_3_sentences: Two studies advanced brain organoid research by examining how organoids record time and develop spatial organization. The findings expand what brain organoids may model in neuroscience.

articles.title: Experimental eye drops help blind mice see again
articles.summary_3_sentences: Light-activated drugs restored light perception and visually guided behavior in blind mice. Some compounds worked as eye drops, but the findings remain preclinical.

articles.title: Scientists discover why damaged nerves struggle to heal
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified AHR as a protein that limits nerve repair. Blocking AHR promoted nerve fiber regrowth and improved movement and sensation in mice with nerve or spinal cord injuries.

articles.title: Your sleep may be hiding an early clue to Alzheimer's
articles.summary_3_sentences: Frequent micro-awakenings during sleep were linked to higher genetic risk for Alzheimer's disease in asymptomatic middle-aged adults. The finding suggests sleep patterns could be studied as early markers.

articles.title: Scientists discover a brain "brake" that can shut down chronic pain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a brain-based system that reduced chronic nerve pain in mice by calming an overactive pain circuit. The work is preclinical and may guide non-opioid pain research.

articles.title: Shingles Vaccine Linked to 24% Lower Dementia Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Older adults who received Shingrix had a 24% lower risk of dementia diagnosis within four years. The report describes an association between shingles vaccination and dementia risk.

articles.title: Ozempic Shows Promise in Bipolar Disorder
articles.summary_3_sentences: Semaglutide was linked to lower psychiatric hospitalization risk in people with bipolar disorder. The visible summary reports an association rather than a proven treatment effect.

articles.title: High-Dose Vitamin D Linked to Better Cognition
articles.summary_3_sentences: Daily vitamin D intake of at least 5,000 IU was associated with better cognitive scores in older adults. The report describes an association and does not establish causality.

articles.title: Speaking Multiple Languages May Slow Brain Aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: Speaking multiple languages was associated with slower brain aging. The visible summary provides limited methodological detail.

articles.title: Personalized brain stimulation can ease chronic pain
articles.summary_3_sentences: A case series of three patients found that week-long brain mapping could guide personalized stimulation for chronic pain relief. The evidence is small and preliminary.

articles.title: Childhood trauma may leave a lasting "scar" inside brain cells
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, early-life stress altered DNA packaging in the brain and primed stress-related genes. Blocking the effect prevented heightened adult anxiety and stress sensitivity in the model.

articles.title: Your brain may not actually "make" decisions
articles.summary_3_sentences: A neuroscientist argues that decision-making may emerge from interactions among perception, movement, the body and the environment rather than a central brain system. The article is conceptual rather than a clinical study.

articles.title: Depression may shut down the brain's ability to make new neurons
articles.summary_3_sentences: A major study reported disrupted hippocampal neurogenesis in adults with depression. Researchers also identified molecular changes that may support more biologically tailored treatments.

articles.title: This common vitamin was linked to 13% better cognitive scores
articles.summary_3_sentences: Older adults with mild cognitive impairment and sleep problems who took at least 5,000 IU of vitamin D daily had higher cognitive test scores. The findings are preliminary and observational in tone.

articles.title: Quitting alcohol may prime the brain for relapse
articles.summary_3_sentences: Mice that developed compulsive drinking after abstinence showed elevated activity in a stress- and addiction-related brain region before relapse. The preclinical signal could help study relapse risk.

articles.title: A major Alzheimer's risk gene may shrink brain cells years before symptoms
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, APOE4 increased Nell2, shrinking neurons and making memory circuits hyperactive before later memory problems. Reducing Nell2 reversed abnormal changes in adult mice.

articles.title: Multilingual people may have brains up to 13 years younger
articles.summary_3_sentences: People speaking several languages had brain-age measures suggesting slower brain aging, with four-language speakers showing the largest reported difference. Earlier start and higher fluency were linked to stronger effects.

articles.title: VR and Scents Boost Mental Health in Isolated Space
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Frontiers in Psychology study examined whether VR nature scenes and scents could support mental health in isolated settings such as spaceflight. The visible summary frames the work around astronaut well-being.

articles.title: Shock wave therapy for erectile dysfunction is on the rise
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports growing use of sound wave-based therapy for erectile dysfunction. The technique is related to shock wave approaches used for kidney stones.

articles.title: An unproven autism drug got a boost after a White House briefing
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that leucovorin dispensing to children rose after a White House briefing promoted it for autism without new evidence. The report concerns policy communication and use of an unproven autism therapy.

articles.title: Schizophrenia's lost brain connections follow a surprising pattern
articles.summary_3_sentences: Specialized brain scans linked schizophrenia to widespread synapse loss, especially on the left side of the brain. The loss followed an organized pattern tied to brain chemistry and wiring.

articles.title: Estrogen Therapy Linked to Lower Dementia Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Later-life estrogen-only hormone therapy was associated with 39% lower odds of clinical dementia diagnosis. The visible summary reports an association, not proof of prevention.

articles.title: AI-designed "intrabodies" could unlock new treatments for Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and MND
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers developed a method to convert antibodies into smaller molecules that work inside human cells. The approach could support research into neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Huntington's and motor neurone disease.

articles.title: Researchers reveal deeper workings of brain's information hub
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that the frontoparietal cortex changes its communication patterns depending on decision-making needs. The network appears to reorganize dynamically rather than simply becoming more active.

articles.title: PlaySmart Game Boosts Teen Mental Health
articles.summary_3_sentences: A JAMA Network Open study examined whether the PlaySmart video game could help treat teen depression. The visible summary presents the game as a mental-health intervention under study.

articles.title: More Screen Time Linked to Better Teen Cognition
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that children with more screen time tended to show better cognitive processing in adolescence. The visible summary notes that the result ran counter to common expectations.

articles.title: Mysterious waves sweeping across your brain may help turn sensory chaos into what you see
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers argue that traveling electrical waves in the brain may help shape attention, prediction, perception and memory. The article presents these waves as a possible computational mechanism.

articles.title: A therapy that "rewrites" childhood memories can ease fear of failure
articles.summary_3_sentences: Young adults who revisited painful childhood memories through imagery-based therapy had lasting reductions in fear, guilt, sadness and stress. The study focused on fear of failure linked to childhood criticism.

articles.title: A little-known protein may be fueling Alzheimer's -- and scientists found a way to block it
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental compound prevented damaging protein clumps and reduced amyloid buildup in mouse brains. The preclinical treatment also affected heart health and aging markers in the report.

articles.title: A little movement in midlife could pay off for your brain years later
articles.summary_3_sentences: Exercise and healthy blood sugar levels in midlife were linked to slower cognitive decline decades later. The report notes physical activity appeared especially beneficial for Mexican American adults.

articles.title: A stress hormone may help the brain repair itself
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that myelin-producing precursor cells release CRH near damaged brain tissue, influencing maturation and repair. The same system may also affect brain development and myelin thickness.

articles.title: Immune cells flood into the aging brain, Stanford scientists discover
articles.summary_3_sentences: Stanford researchers found that immune cells from the blood enter the human brain as early as middle age and can become microglia-like cells. The finding challenges assumptions about separation between brain and body immunity.

articles.title: Women taking estrogen had fewer signs of Alzheimer's in their brains
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a large study, later-life estrogen-only hormone therapy was associated with lower dementia odds and fewer Alzheimer's-related brain changes. Biomarker tests also suggested less amyloid among hormone therapy users.

articles.title: Human brain cells are far more powerful than scientists thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that individual human cortical neurons can perform complex computations. The report suggests single neurons may contribute more to cognition than simple on-off models imply.

articles.title: The adult brain can repair itself better than scientists thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, specialized astrocytes responded to brain damage by creating new nuclei and sending them into damaged regions. The finding is preclinical and suggests a repair mechanism in adult brain tissue.

articles.title: Modifiable Risks Linked to Dementia-Related Brain Damage
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports links between modifiable risks, such as smoking and high blood pressure, and dementia-related brain damage. It notes that nearly half of dementia cases may involve modifiable risk factors.

articles.title: Ozempic may have revealed the brain's hidden "craving center"
articles.summary_3_sentences: Ozempic-like drugs may reduce cravings for alcohol and other addictive substances, with attention focused on the lateral septum. The report links GLP-1 receptors in this region to reward-seeking behavior.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden brain rhythm that could improve Parkinson's treatment
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a brain network and electrical rhythm linked to benefits from deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease. The finding could support more personalized stimulation settings.

articles.title: Scientists discover the brain has a fast lane and slow lane for clearing waste
articles.summary_3_sentences: AI-assisted measurements showed that brain fluid moves quickly around outer spaces but much more slowly through deep tissue. The findings may inform studies of Alzheimer's, aging and concussion-related circulation problems.

articles.title: MIT neuroscientists discover the brain can reason without words
articles.summary_3_sentences: MIT researchers found evidence that language and logical reasoning rely on separate brain systems. People with severe language impairments could solve logic puzzles, while language regions stayed mostly quiet during reasoning tasks.

articles.title: Scientists say just 7 days of meditation can rewire your brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: An intensive seven-day meditation retreat was linked to changes in brain and body measures involving neuroplasticity, immunity, metabolism and pain relief. Participants also showed connectivity patterns compared with psychedelic-associated states.

articles.title: Stress can scramble your brain's internal GPS, MRI study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: An MRI study found that cortisol disrupted grid-cell activity and worsened navigation in a virtual environment. The effect was strongest when landmarks were absent.

articles.title: Teen cannabis use linked to slower memory and thinking growth
articles.summary_3_sentences: Teen cannabis use was linked to slower growth in memory, attention, language and processing speed. THC was identified as the most likely driver, especially for memory effects.

articles.title: New autism therapy shows surprising benefits even in adult mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: Blocking SLC6A20 improved signaling and autism-related behaviors in mouse models and worked in human brain organoids. The findings are preclinical and do not establish effectiveness in people.

articles.title: THC medication made PTSD nightmares disappear for more than a third of patients
articles.summary_3_sentences: A prescription THC medication reduced PTSD-related nightmares, with more than one-third of patients reporting disappearance after ten weeks. The article describes a potential treatment for a persistent PTSD symptom.

articles.title: Scientists discover the brain cells that keep you motivated
articles.summary_3_sentences: In rats, orexin neurons helped sustain motivation when rewards became harder to obtain. Blocking the cells reduced goal-directed persistence.

articles.title: Two new compounds could reveal hidden drivers of Alzheimer's disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers created a selective TAOK-1 inhibitor and another compound that activates the TAOK protein family. These tools may help study Alzheimer's mechanisms and identify treatment strategies.

articles.title: Scientists may have found aging's hidden trigger for brain disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: In worms, age-related buildup of EPS8 promoted toxic protein aggregation, neuronal damage and shorter lifespan. Reducing EPS8 preserved nerve function in the model.

articles.title: The Gut Microbiome is Linked to Memory Formation
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports a link between the gut microbiome and memory formation. The visible summary frames body microbes as relevant to how memories are understood.

topic_groups.topic: Infectious Disease, Vaccines and Immune Health

articles.title: FDA Approves Gilead's New Once-Daily HIV Pill Bixlenvo
articles.summary_3_sentences: The FDA approved Bixlenvo as a once-daily oral combination pill for virologically suppressed adults with HIV. The article reports the approval of Gilead's new HIV medication.

articles.title: Novel Strategy to Enhance Zika Virus Vaccination
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports a novel strategy intended to enhance Zika virus vaccination. The visible summary places the work in the context of decades of Zika spread.

articles.title: Fallowed Farms Linked to Valley Fever Spikes
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Science Advances study linked California land-use shifts, including fallowed farms, to valley fever spikes. The article concerns environmental drivers of fungal disease patterns.

articles.title: Bird flu is spreading. Your backyard feeder could make it worse
articles.summary_3_sentences: Experts warned that backyard bird feeders could create H5N1 hotspots by bringing bird species together. The article recommends stopping feeding as safest, with hygiene and reduced feeding as risk-reduction steps.

articles.title: AI may know how you'll respond to a vaccine before you get it
articles.summary_3_sentences: AI analysis of antibody patterns in more than 4,000 people identified signals of immune readiness before vaccination. The report suggests potential prediction of strong and weak vaccine responses.

articles.title: Why Epstein-Barr is the 'everything virus'
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reviews Epstein-Barr virus and its broad health burden. It highlights links to conditions including multiple sclerosis and cancer.

articles.title: No refrigerator, no problem. This experimental vaccine doesn't need it.
articles.summary_3_sentences: Early trials found that an experimental vaccine not requiring refrigeration still protected against tetanus and diphtheria. The finding may be relevant to vaccine storage and distribution.

articles.title: COVID-19 awakens dormant viruses -- and one is linked to long COVID
articles.summary_3_sentences: COVID-19 was reported to reactivate dormant viruses including Epstein-Barr, cytomegalovirus and herpes viruses. One poorly understood viral family was strongly associated with long COVID and disability.

articles.title: How a brutal drought may have helped unleash yellow fever in Brazil
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that drought may have driven animals toward cities in Brazil, possibly contributing to a yellow fever outbreak. It links ecological disruption to infectious disease risk.

articles.title: A surprising triple treatment completely clears hiv in newborn primates
articles.summary_3_sentences: Newborn nonhuman primates treated within three days of HIV exposure cleared virus after a one-time combination of antiretrovirals, broadly neutralizing antibodies and leronlimab. The finding is preclinical and none of the components worked alone.

articles.title: A New Strategy to Tackle Drug-Resistant Gonorrhea
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article presents a strategy for drug-resistant gonorrhea that may also apply to other resistant bacterial pathogens. The visible summary focuses on antimicrobial resistance.

articles.title: Peroxisome structure can help protect insulin and maintain beta cell health
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a role for peroxisomes in protecting insulin and maintaining pancreatic beta cell health and maturity. The finding concerns basic mechanisms relevant to insulin-producing cells.

articles.title: A common vape flavoring may disrupt early embryo development
articles.summary_3_sentences: In lab experiments, vanillin used in e-cigarette flavoring disrupted embryonic stem cell developmental potential. The study is laboratory-based and does not directly establish pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Common medications may change your gut for years
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of more than 2,500 people linked past use of antibiotics, antidepressants, beta-blockers, acid-reducing drugs and benzodiazepines to long-lasting gut microbiome changes. Some effects were detectable years later.

articles.title: Scientists discover how gut bacteria "train" the intestine to fight inflammation
articles.summary_3_sentences: Butyrate, produced when gut bacteria break down fiber, reprogrammed intestinal lining cells toward anti-inflammatory responses. In mice, the effect increased IL-10 and reduced colitis-like disease severity.

articles.title: The Gut Microbiome Impacts Uterine Inflammation and Female Reproductive Health
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Journal of Advanced Research study reported that maternal gut dysbiosis increases uterine inflammation. The article frames the finding within female reproductive health.

articles.title: Genetic map of IBS expands beyond the gut-brain axis
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that genetic studies of irritable bowel syndrome are expanding beyond nervous-system-focused explanations. The visible summary provides limited detail about the new genetic map.

articles.title: A light-based scan could detect deadly bowel disease in preterm babies
articles.summary_3_sentences: A proposed light-based scan aims to detect necrotizing enterocolitis early in premature babies. The article describes the approach as quick and low-risk.

articles.title: How Plant-Based Foods Boost the Gut Microbiome & Human Health
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes how plant-based foods may benefit health partly through effects on gut microorganisms. The visible summary presents broad microbiome-related dietary benefits.

articles.title: How Metaproteomics Can Advance Gut Microbiome Research
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article explains how metaproteomics can help study the human gut microbiome. It notes that gut microorganisms have been linked to many health conditions.

articles.title: 3D Genome Mapping Reveals New Crohn's Disease Insights
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that 3D genome mapping revealed new insights into Crohn's disease. It emphasizes genome organization inside the nucleus as relevant to disease understanding.

articles.title: Allergy-Reducing Bacteria are Identified
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified bacteria that may help explain the reduced allergy risk observed in children raised in rural environments. The article links the finding to the farm effect.

topic_groups.topic: Pregnancy, Pediatrics, Development and Social Health

articles.title: Assessment of culinary skills among adults with visual impairment highlights gaps between ability and independence
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Journal of Nutrition Education and Behavior study found adults with visual impairment often had medium or high culinary skills but still faced barriers to kitchen independence. The report highlights accessible tools and training.

articles.title: Childhood adversity may put women at higher risk for postpartum depression years later
articles.summary_3_sentences: A George Mason-led study found women with multiple adverse childhood experiences reported the highest postpartum depressive symptoms. Despite higher risk, they were not more likely to receive postpartum depression screening.

articles.title: Physical exams alone may not reliably diagnose pneumonia in children, national study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A national pediatric study found that clinicians may not consistently hear or interpret the same lung findings when examining children with possible pneumonia. The report highlights limitations of physical examination alone.

articles.title: Studies reveal how instability may shape infant attention, brain activity and emotional regulation
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports studies on how environmental instability may shape infant attention, brain activity and emotional regulation. The visible summary emphasizes that infants continue learning in chaotic conditions.

articles.title: AI Predicts Pregnancy Risks Early in Global 500k-Data Study
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Journal of Medical Internet Research study used global data from 500,000 cases to examine AI prediction of pregnancy risks. The report focuses on early identification using artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Researchers followed 400,000 kids for 20 years and found a lasting pre-K advantage
articles.summary_3_sentences: A 20-year study of 400,000 students found public-school pre-K attendance was linked to better grades and test scores through high school. Teacher training and structured classroom exposure were suggested as possible contributors.

articles.title: Mini-brains show how maternal inflammation alters development
articles.summary_3_sentences: Brain organoid models were used to study how maternal inflammation alters developmental processes. The visible summary does not identify a specific inflammatory pathway.

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years -- the screen time result was unexpected
articles.summary_3_sentences: An eight-year Finnish study found children with more screen time tended to show better cognitive processing as teenagers. Researchers suggested that the type of screen activity and balance with physical activity may matter.

articles.title: Common food preservative linked to rising suicide deaths among young people
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers linked a widely available food-preservation chemical to rising UK suicide deaths, especially among young people and men. They called for restrictions on access and harmful online information.

topic_groups.topic: Biomedical Tools, AI, Imaging and Basic Cell Science

articles.title: Spatial Tissue Imaging Gets an Upgrade with PASTA
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers advanced spatial tissue imaging using a workflow called PASTA. The report describes improvements in spatial profiling technology from a team including Harvard scientists and collaborators.

articles.title: Satellite Cell Readiness is Governed by an RNA-Binding Protein in Muscle
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Stem Cell Reports study identified TDP-43 as important for muscle satellite cell readiness. The finding concerns regulation of muscle stem-cell function.

articles.title: New Tool for Imaging Cristae Structure & Electrical Flickers
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers introduced a tool to image mitochondrial cristae structure and electrical dynamics. The method addresses challenges in visualizing inner mitochondrial membrane ultrastructure and activity.

articles.title: GenAI creates first fully functional synthetic virus genomes
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers at Stanford University and the Arc Institute used generative AI to design fully functional synthetic virus genomes. The work demonstrates AI-based genome design capability.

articles.title: EasyGrid Simplifies Cryo-Electron Microscopy Sample Preparation
articles.summary_3_sentences: EasyGrid, reported in Nature Methods, simplifies cryo-electron microscopy sample preparation. The method reduces guesswork and time-consuming optimization.

articles.title: A hidden "on switch" in human DNA has finally been decoded
articles.summary_3_sentences: AI analysis of about 500,000 DNA sequences identified the initiator signature in roughly 60% of human genes. The finding may help predict mutation effects and gene-activity instructions.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Sheds Light on How Our Immune System Functions
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers are applying artificial intelligence to better understand immune-system functions. The visible summary frames the work as part of broader AI progress.

articles.title: Exercise releases protective, muscle-strengthening molecule
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that exercise releases a molecule that enhances muscle function and performance. The visible summary identifies protective and muscle-strengthening effects.

articles.title: Human-Guided AI Speeds Up Cell Classification for Spatial Proteomics
articles.summary_3_sentences: Human-guided AI was used to speed cell classification in spatial proteomics. The approach addresses analysis of multiplexed tissue images and protein signals.

articles.title: Japanese scientists use tiny silver particles to make DNA assembly up to 5x more efficient
articles.summary_3_sentences: Silver nanoparticles were used to cut DNA and create longer sticky ends, improving fragment assembly efficiency. The method could aid construction of large DNA sequences for biomedical and agricultural applications.

articles.title: Tiny robots powered by light can hunt down and collect bacteria
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers built light-driven microrobots that move through liquid, collect bacteria and deposit them in selected locations. The technology could support precise manipulation of microbes and cells.

articles.title: Clues to longevity may reside in the genomes of long-lived bats
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers are sequencing bat genomes to look for clues to their exceptional longevity relative to body size. The work focuses on basic comparative genomics rather than human intervention testing.

articles.title: Seven new frog species were hiding beneath Madagascar's forest floor
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified seven new Madagascar diamond frog species using DNA from modern and museum specimens. The discovery reveals hidden biodiversity relevant to conservation.

articles.title: Dogs may hold surprising clues to human longevity
articles.summary_3_sentences: The Dog Aging Project linked blood-metabolite patterns in dogs to longer or shorter lifespans. Similarities with human aging signatures may help study aging biology.

articles.title: Bat Genetics Provide Insight into Longevity
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers examined bat genetics to investigate how bats achieve long lifespans for their body size. The article presents comparative genetics as a route to understanding longevity.

articles.title: Your dislike of eating bugs may be 9,000 years old
articles.summary_3_sentences: Ancient teeth and DNA suggest northern Eurasian modern humans ate insects only occasionally, while Neanderthals may have eaten them more regularly. Populations near the tropics retained genes aiding insect exoskeleton digestion.

articles.title: 190-year-old DNA reveals a hidden pangolin species
articles.summary_3_sentences: DNA from a nearly 190-year-old museum specimen helped confirm a distinct Himalayan pangolin species. The finding may assist conservation and tracking of illegal pangolin trade.

articles.title: Scientists find hidden "highways" guiding animal evolution
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large analysis of animal genomes suggested chromosome evolution follows a limited set of irreversible pathways. The finding offers clues to more than 600 million years of animal evolution.

articles.title: People who live past 110 have an unusual abundance of killer immune cells
articles.summary_3_sentences: Supercentenarians were reported to have unusually high numbers of CD4 cytotoxic T cells. The cells expanded with age, suggesting repeated immune responses to persistent threats.

articles.title: This shark can live 400 years. Its eyes barely seem to age
articles.summary_3_sentences: Greenland sharks showed healthy eye tissue and active blue-light proteins despite lifespans that can reach centuries. The study may offer clues for research on vision and aging.

articles.title: This gut microbe may help keep you strong as you age
articles.summary_3_sentences: Roseburia inulinivorans was linked to stronger muscles in older adults and mice. Treated mice had greater grip strength and larger fast-twitch muscle fibers.

articles.title: A mother's age can shape her offspring without changing their DNA
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported that maternal age effects on offspring may involve reversible changes in gene activity rather than permanent DNA damage. The article discusses possible multigenerational influences.

articles.title: Tiny 1.7-billion-year-old fossils could reveal how complex life began
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists are examining ancient fossils to study how complex life evolved from microbial origins. The work may also inform questions about complex life on other worlds.

articles.title: Animals have been eating nature's original bioplastic for millions of years
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that many animals have enzymes capable of breaking down microbial bioplastics called PHAs. The finding suggests animals have been consuming natural bioplastics for long evolutionary periods.

articles.title: A 60-year-old theory about ants, bees and wasps may be wrong
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large analysis challenged the idea that an unusual genetic system alone explains social colonies in ants, bees and wasps. The article suggests other insect traits may be important.

articles.title: Neanderthal gene linked to more muscle mass in modern humans
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Neanderthal-derived gene was linked to higher muscle mass in some modern humans. The article focuses on inherited genetic variation and muscle traits.

articles.title: Paleontology rocked by organic molecules found in 66-million-year-old dinosaur bones
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported evidence that original collagen can survive in dinosaur fossils for tens of millions of years. The discovery may provide molecular clues about dinosaur biology and fossilization.

articles.title: Scientists find evidence for two origins of life on Earth
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers studying life's origins found evidence that free-living cells may have emerged twice. The article presents a hypothesis about early cellular evolution and the genetic code.

articles.title: For 15,000 years, humans and dogs have been changing each other
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reviews 15,000 years of coevolution between humans and dogs. It highlights adaptations to different environments and human needs.

articles.title: Scientists find unexpected life on Ötzi the Iceman's 5,300-year-old body
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers separated microbes present during Ötzi's life from those that arrived after death. They found traces of ancient gut bacteria and cold-loving yeasts preserved with the Iceman.

articles.title: Forget the sperm race: Fertilization may depend on teamwork
articles.summary_3_sentences: An evolutionary study found sperm cooperation is widespread among arthropods and has repeatedly evolved and disappeared. The finding challenges simple competition-only views of fertilization.

articles.title: Scientists catch a "jumping gene" mid-leap between species
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found circular intron RNA from a predatory bacterium inside dead cells of another microorganism. The stable RNA ring may represent a route for mobile genetic elements to move between species.

topic_groups.topic: Drug Approvals, Biopharma, Policy and Safety

articles.title: FDA authorizes first wearable to track both ketones and blood sugar
articles.summary_3_sentences: The FDA authorized a wearable device that tracks both ketones and blood sugar. The device is intended to warn people with diabetes when a dangerous complication begins to develop.

articles.title: FDA Approves First Targeted Therapy for Rare Skin Disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: The FDA approved Priovant's brepocitinib, marketed as Lisraya, for adults with dermatomyositis. The article describes it as the first targeted therapy for the rare skin disease.

articles.title: FDA Approves Pasatru for Rare Bone-Forming Disorder
articles.summary_3_sentences: The FDA approved Regeneron's Pasatru for a rare bone-forming disorder. The treatment is intended to reduce abnormal new bone formation and clinician-assessed flare-ups.

articles.title: Novo Nordisk Tests Lower-Dose Wegovy Pill for Weight Loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: Novo Nordisk is testing lower maintenance doses of a Wegovy pill in a placebo-controlled trial. The study examines whether lower doses can still support weight loss.

articles.title: Obsidian Therapeutics Merges with Galera Therapeutics
articles.summary_3_sentences: Obsidian Therapeutics completed a merger transaction involving Galera Therapeutics. Obsidian is described as a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company.

articles.title: The Merger of Radiopharmaceutical Pioneering Companies: Curium and Lantheus
articles.summary_3_sentences: Curium and Lantheus announced plans to merge their businesses. Both companies are described as leaders in nuclear medicine and radiopharmaceuticals.

articles.title: Fresenius Recalls Tyenne Over Glass Particle Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Fresenius Kabi recalled 20 ml vials of Tyenne, a tocilizumab-aazg injection. The recall was due to a glass-particle risk found through an internal investigation.

articles.title: Trump Orders Major Overhaul of Childhood Vaccines
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports an order called Gold Standard Childhood Vaccine Recommendations that would lower the number of universally recommended shots. The visible summary identifies the order as issued by Trump.

topic_groups.topic: Environmental Health, Occupational and Ecosystem Science

articles.title: Your skin chemistry may affect which mosquitoes most want to bite you
articles.summary_3_sentences: Three mosquito species preferred different people based on skin odor and bacteria. The findings could support development of microbe-based repellents.

articles.title: Pollen has a surprising problem -- and honeybees have found a way around it
articles.summary_3_sentences: Honeybees appear to detect nutrient imbalances in pollen and adjust intake to avoid excesses. They also transform pollen into balanced larval food.

articles.title: Schools Must Treat Heat Waves Like a Snow Day for Cognition
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses a report on how schools should adapt to increasing heat waves because of effects on cognition. The visible summary frames heat waves as an education and health concern.

articles.title: Scientists Warn Marine Heatwaves Cause Mental, Body Harm
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Nature Sustainability study examined how marine heatwaves affect human health. The article reports mental and physical harms associated with ocean heatwaves.

articles.title: Scientists discover bacteria that lock toxic uranium into a stable form
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that bacteria in uranium-contaminated mine water could convert dissolved uranium into a stable compound when fed glycerol. About 95% of dissolved uranium disappeared within 130 days in the reported experiment.

articles.title: World's most-used weedkiller disrupts honeybee brains
articles.summary_3_sentences: Glyphosate-exposed honeybees foraged less and showed brain chemical changes linked to behavior after three days. The article raises concerns about hive health and pollination.

articles.title: New philosophical framework reframes moral distress in health care
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes a philosophical framework for understanding moral distress among nurses and physicians. It focuses on situations where clinicians know what care is needed but face external barriers.

articles.title: The dental crown of the future could be 3D-printed while you wait
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reduced 3D-printed zirconia crown processing time from up to 100 hours to under 30 minutes. The advance could eventually enable same-appointment permanent dental crowns.

articles.title: Weak Electrical Signals Send Aging Muscle into Decline
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that weak electrical signals contribute to age-related muscle decline. It suggests muscle wasting may be reversible with targeted pharmaceuticals.

articles.title: What Spider-Man gets right -- and wrong -- about turning off superpowers
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article uses a Spider-Man storyline to discuss a fictional superpower inhibitor based on real RNA therapy concepts. It is a science explainer connected to RNA-based treatments.

articles.title: Tiny 1.7-billion-year-old fossils could reveal how complex life began
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists are studying some of Earth's oldest rocks for fossils that could illuminate the emergence of complex life. The work may also inform astrobiology questions.

articles.title: The common mistake that could make aging joints hurt more
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article explains that avoiding movement can worsen joint problems with aging. Low-impact exercise may nourish cartilage, strengthen supporting muscles and reduce osteoarthritis pain.

articles.title: Knee osteoarthritis isn't inevitable -- here's what you can do
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that exercise, stronger leg muscles, healthier diet and modest weight loss can reduce knee stress and help manage osteoarthritis pain. It presents modifiable approaches rather than a single trial result.

articles.title: Scientists solve the mystery of a brain "switch" that can trigger weight loss in opposite ways
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, activating GIP receptors in one brain region and blocking them in another both promoted weight loss through different mechanisms. The finding may inform GLP-1 and GIP-targeting obesity drugs.

articles.title: Immune Cell Reprogramming Eliminates the Need to Treat Poultry with Antibiotics
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that immune-cell reprogramming could eliminate the need to treat poultry with antibiotics. The finding is framed as an alternative approach in poultry production.

articles.title: THC Drug Reduces PTSD Nightmares
articles.summary_3_sentences: Dronabinol, a prescription form of THC, reduced the frequency and intensity of PTSD-related nightmares. The article focuses on symptom reduction in PTSD.

articles.title: Dogs can tell fear from sadness -- and scientists saw it in their brains
articles.summary_3_sentences: Brain scans suggested dogs respond differently to human emotional expressions, with happy faces activating reward-related regions. The findings concern animal cognition and human-animal communication.

articles.title: Obesity-related muscle wasting linked to a key immune signal
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers linked obesity-related skeletal muscle wasting and strength loss to a key immune signal. The article frames the condition as sarcopenia associated with obesity.

articles.title: A drug already used for osteoporosis blocked spinal damage in a new study
articles.summary_3_sentences: Zebrafish with a collagen-related gene defect developed spinal changes resembling human disc disease. An existing osteoporosis drug and fat-metabolism targeting reduced damage in the model.

articles.title: Nearly half of dementia cases may be linked to risks you can change
articles.summary_3_sentences: A long-term brain study linked smoking, high blood pressure, heart disease and high blood lipids to vascular dementia-related damage. The findings support attention to modifiable risks.

articles.title: Two deadly flowers could inspire powerful new medicines
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified enzymes used by wolfsbane and larkspur to make atisinium, a compound with possible medical potential. They recreated the pathway in tobacco plants for sustainable production and testing.
